title: Investigate retry-amplification across proxy pools causing anomalous billing spike for enterprise customer
creator: Iris Chen
description: Support escalation from a single enterprise customer (Acme Financials) reporting a 9x month-over-month billed token increase. Investigation focused on billing/metering pipeline, rate limiter behavior, and proxy pool retries. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigations, and credits issued.
incident_timeline: 2025-11-03: Customer support ticket opened by Acme Financials reporting an unexpected $12k spike for October usage.
2025-11-04: Initial billing report generated; on-call review flagged elevated success counts for their API key between 2025-10-12 and 2025-10-16.
2025-11-05: Eng on-call confirmed elevated completion counts correlated with increased 502/504 errors from edge proxies earlier in the day.
2025-11-06: Reproducer built in staging that simulated transient proxy timeouts and measured request completion duplication in metering.
2025-11-07: Hotfix deployed to billing ingest to deduplicate completions by request_id for 48h backfill window.
2025-11-10: Postback reconciliation run; credits and customer communication drafted.
2025-11-14: Full roll-forward fix merged that prevents retry amplification at proxy layer and adds stricter dedupe and telemetry.
2025-11-18: Credits applied and ticket closed after customer acceptance.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Originate a burst of requests through proxy-pool A with an artificially introduced 50-200ms timeout on backend connections.
2) Configure client to retry on 502/504 with idempotent request semantics but without a stable request_id header.

3) Observe that some retries successfully complete and are recorded as separate completions in metering, because the original request also eventually completes and has no shared dedupe key in the ingest pipeline.
4) Repeat across multiple proxy instances to simulate cross-pool counter resets which exacerbate counting anomalies.
findings: Metering pipeline counted multiple successful completions for the same logical user request because request-level deduplication depended on an optional request_id header that was not consistently set by the customer SDK.

Proxy pool retry behavior amplified the count: when a backend connection timed out, proxy retried the request to a different backend without propagating a stable request_id, resulting in multiple distinct completions across replicas.

A short-lived race condition in the ingest stream’s shard assignment caused two collectors to momentarily accept the same completion and both emit it to the billing counter. This happened when the collectors rebalanced during the amplified retry window.
Customer integration used client-side retries with exponential backoff but with high max attempts; combined with proxy retries this produced up to 9x observed completions for certain bursts.

No existing automatic detection flagged the spike because total request rate was within historical bounds; only per-key completion-to-request ratio and duplicate request_id signals revealed the anomaly.
root_cause: A conjunction of three issues: (1) lack of enforced request-level deduplication in the billing ingest for optional request_id, (2) proxy-layer retry behavior that could reissue requests without propagating a stable id, and (3) transient collector shard rebalances that caused duplicate emission of completions. Together these allowed retry-amplification to be recorded as distinct billable completions.
immediate_mitigation: Backfill dedupe: run a 48-hour backfill to collapse completions with matching client_ip, timestamp window, and best-effort request fingerprint into single billable events.
Hotfix deployed: billing ingest now treats missing request_id as dedupeable and uses a fingerprint heuristic to prevent obvious duplicates for 72h.
Temporary quota cap: applied an account-level soft cap for Acme Financials to prevent further runaway charges while investigation proceeded.
Customer communication: notified Acme of findings and proposed credit amount for initial review.
long_term_actions: Require stable request_id header in SDKs and make server-side enforcement opt-out for enterprise customers (Feature): owners: SDK team / PM Helena Park.
Proxy change: ensure retries always include the original request_id when present; add id propagation tests in proxy integration suite. Owner: infra/proxy (Marco Alvarado).
Ingest hardening: add cross-shard deduplication window in billing pipeline and stronger idempotency guarantees. Owner: billing team (Rohit Sen).
Observability: add a dedicated alert on completion_count / issued_requests ratio per API key and on per-key duplicate_id rate. Owner: SRE (Ana Gomez).
Post-deployment validation: schedule canary checks for billing delta anomalies after infra or proxy releases.
credits_issued: $12,450 credited to Acme Financials (applied 2025-11-18). Credit breakdown included full refund for duplicated completions identified in backfill and a goodwill credit for operational impact.
